attrs.evidence: A bridge block with TWO separators. Site 0 pins v1 = 0 through an OR/NAND triangle, site 1 pins v2 = 0 through another, site 2 holds v1 ≠ v2. Every pairwise intersection at v1 and at v2 is non-empty, every site is satisfiable, κₛ = 0 — and the union has no model, because the bridge block needs the JOINT restriction at both ends. The two-pass protocol catches it. Pairwise agreement is necessary and not sufficient.
attrs.statement: Pairwise non-empty intersection of the sites' projections at each shared separator variable is sufficient for union satisfiability.
